name: Panteleus
bio: Panteleus is known to the Greek Anthology only as the author of one epigram in the Planudean Appendix. Paton’s Index of Authors gives no date for him.
This archive carries the 1 epigram ascribed to the poet in the fifth volume of W. R. Paton's prose translation (Loeb, 1918): Book XVI: 6a.

poems.title: Book XVI, 6a: On Callimachus and Cynaegirus, the Athenian Captains at Marathon
poems.author: Panteleus
poems.text: O empty toil and ineffective war! What shall we say when we meet our King? O King, why didst thou send me against immortal warriors? We shoot them and they fall not, we wound them and they fear not. A single man laid low a whole host, and covered with blood he stands in the midst, the image of tireless Ares; he stands like a tree with iron roots and will not fall, and soon he will be in the ships. Loose the cable, captain; let us escape from the dead man’s threats.
